newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-C&W says banks on shareholder value.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-C&W says banks on shareholder value.

text.p: Cable and Wireless, the British parent of Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd, said on Friday it would only take a stake in China Telecom if a deal enhanced shareholder value and if "important projects in mainland China" were realised.

"Any further steps in a second phase will be driven entirely by sharehoder value -- as we judge it and, if necessary, as our shareholders will judge it," deputy chief executive Rod Olsen told reporters by telephone from Beijing.
C&W earlier ended months of speculation by selling a 5.5 percent stake for HK$14.25 per share in its main Hong Kong asset to the Chinese.

C&W's long-expected sale of part of its 59 percent stake in the strategically important Hong Kong Telecom, which raises 726 million stg, leaves the British company with a majority stake -- at least for the time being.
China Telecom (Hong Kong) is the vehicle set up by China to exploit capital markets and assist in the growth of telecommunications in China and to develop the Hong Kong market.
The 5.5 percent stake sale will not be technically complete ahead of the July 1 handover of Hong Kong to Chinese rule and any second phase had been left open-ended, Olsen said.
"There is a great deal of work to do to define opportunity in mainland China and to build China Telecom (Hong Kong)," Olsen said.
The company said it did have its eye on specific projects in China, which might include taking equity stakes, but declined to give details. No further deals were expected before July 1, Olsen said.

Olsen also did not rule out further investments in Britain, where some analysts have speculated that C&W may use disposal proceeds to buy out the 50 percent stake U S West has in its cellular operator, One2One.

"I don't think you could expect us to speculate on what other opportunities we might have -- but we are not short of ideas and opportunities to dig our roots deeper in our markets where we do have a presence around the world and to grow shareholder value," he said.
Chief executive Richard Brown called the deal a "unique opportunity", but added that no single telecoms group would have exclusive rights to developing the telecommunications market in China.
"You wouldn't expect China to offer any single telecom carrier in development work in China an exclusive right to that work," he said.
"But this is a representation of the first significant occasion where a foreign telecommunications company has been invited into substantial work in mainland China."
Asked where the main opportunities lay in China, Brown said that in a country where only six households in every 100 have a telephone "anything you can conceive is opportunity".
"I think one of the attractiveness is that in Hong Kong Telecom, we have a superior example of the most advanced telecom technology in the world, superior customer service..." he said.

Brown also noted this deal in China further enhanced the attractiveness of C&W to potential world alliances, such as the Global One partnership of Deutsche Telekom AG, France Telecom and America's Sprint Corp or AT&T Corp's World Partners/Unisource alliances.
"What we may or may not do with any global alliance, we'll decide at the right time and I can only tell you -- no door is closed to us," he said.
Brown declined to comment on whether any French government decision to abandon a minority sell-off of France Telecom made Global One less attractive.
